name: Ibn Durayd
bio: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Durayd al-Azdi, of the Azd of Oman, was born in Basra in 223 AH (838 CE) and became one of the great authorities on the Arabic language; Ibn Khallikan reports that earlier scholars called him “the most learned of poets and the most poetic of the learned”. He left Basra when the Zanj rose and lived twelve years in Oman, then went to Fars, where the two Mikalis who governed it put him in charge of its chancery; he compiled his dictionary al-Jamhara for them and praised them in his Maqsura, for which they gave him ten thousand dirhams. In 308 AH he moved to Baghdad, where, al-Zirikli writes in al-A'lam, the caliph al-Muqtadir granted him fifty dinars a month. He was struck by paralysis at about ninety and died in Baghdad in 321 AH (933 CE) on the same day as the theologian Abu Hashim al-Jubba'i, and people said, Ibn Khallikan records, “Today the science of language and the science of theology died.”
